item.title: Global Recorded Music Retail Revenue to Top $121 Billion by 2033, MIDiA Report Says
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest trends and forecasts in the music industry. Today, we're looking at the future of recorded music revenues. According to a new report by MIDiA, the global recorded music market is expected to grow by 62.9% to $121.1 billion by 2033.
[Soft background music continues]
Host: That's a significant increase from $74.3 billion in 2025. But what's driving this growth? The report suggests that while streaming will continue to be a major contributor, expanded rights - including revenue from branding, merchandise, and live events - will become the second-fastest growing source of revenue.
[Short audio clip of a music festival or live event]
Host: In fact, MIDiA predicts that the "fan economy" could reach $18.5 billion by 2033. This includes revenue from physical music sales, streaming from social and gaming platforms, and expanded rights from areas like branding and merchandise.
[Soft background music continues]
Host: The report also forecasts that retail growth will outpace trade growth, with music retail revenues expected to reach $62.7 billion by 2033. This means that subscription pricing will likely evolve in the coming years, leading to a return to growth for subscription average revenue per user.
[Outro music starts playing]
Host: That's all for today's podcast. Thanks for tuning in to our discussion on the future of recorded music revenues. Join us next time for more insights and trends in the music industry.
[Outro music continues to play until the end]
